title: RML-G1 supplied-gold recurrent action fast falsifier
summary: Add the smallest model-facing RML gate that isolates the downstream organism: a frozen 32B resolver receives target-independent supplied-gold local memory through at most four adaptive one-hop reads and must execute the existing nine-action J/P targets. The gate compares recurrent access with no-memory, fixed-open, atoms-only, complete-cut, and twin-binding controls. It is an engineering and construct-validity gate only; DREAM, SLEEP, LoRA, independent lifetime sampling, and paper claims remain forbidden.
system_thesis: Before testing whether experience can be dreamed or compressed into weights, establish that correct connected experiential structure can causally change a frozen agent's later actions through the intended recurrent read-think-act interface. A failure localizes the problem downstream of writing; a pass licenses, but does not prove, the learned-text rung.

context_files.purpose: Verbatim owner instructions requiring rigorous paper-first design, useful quick tests, persistence, and eventual GPU execution without treating engineering as science.
Binding architecture deliberation, exact ratification, independent review, and pre-GPU authority contract.
Adjudicated synthesis of the paper architecture, evidence ladder, corrected call count, baselines, gates, and stop rules.
Paper-facing causal lifetime benchmark and baseline requirements retained beyond this diagnostic.
Earlier G1/G2 hybrid contract used only where reconciled by the current synthesis.
Passing CPU fixture report establishing the deterministic source schedule and J/P diagnostic inventory, not model evidence.
Independent audit recommending the supplied-gold recurrent action gate and exposing D0's single-fixture limits.
Implementation reuse map and corrected per-trajectory model-call accounting.
Cross-critique selecting a text-first action gate before LoRA and bounding the pilot's scientific interpretation.
Prior-art and minimum-baseline audit preventing broad novelty or memory-superiority claims from this gate.

nodes.before: The tested generic thinker can query memory but does not execute the RML environment's action protocol.
nodes.after: An isolated frozen resolver emits exactly one READ or legal environment action per model call, carries a bounded scratch state, and terminates after at most four reads and nine action calls.
nodes.rationale: This is the missing downstream organ needed to test whether supplied connected memory can affect behavior.

nodes.before: RML-D0 has symbolic certificates but no model-facing condition-matched memory interface.
nodes.after: A target-independent read-only service exposes condition-specific rows under NONE, GOLD, ATOMS, CUT, and TWIN transforms while logging exact keys, returns, provenance, and masks.
nodes.rationale: Matched access and causal transforms distinguish memory use from model priors, fixed dumping, lookup, or leakage.

edges.before: No tested RML edge carries a memory return into an action-capable recurrent controller.
edges.after: Each authorized one-hop return updates the next resolver state; the model may adapt the next key or emit the next legal action, and every credited action path must cite decisive returned rows.
edges.rationale: The paper architecture requires memory to change intermediate reasoning and later action, not merely answer a post-hoc query.

edges.before: The D0 oracle scores symbolic registered controllers only.
edges.after: After the trajectory freezes, the unchanged offline oracle scores executed actions, path validity, cited support, cut dependence, and twin redirection without feeding any result back to the model.
edges.rationale: Outcome scoring must be causally downstream and absent from the cognitive loop.

loops.before: No model-facing RML loop adaptively alternates local memory reads and real environment actions.
loops.after: For one sealed target side and one blinded condition, start from identical clean model state; allow at most four sequential one-hop READ operations and exactly the bounded public action protocol, one operation per 32B call; record all prompts, outputs, state transitions, keys, returns, citations, actions, invalids, and token costs; freeze before offline scoring.
loops.trigger: The exact change is human-ratified, the implementation packet passes CPU tests and leak checks, and independent reviewer plus author-side advocate approve it.
reads: sealed public target and current public environment state
bounded resolver scratch and prior public operation trace
writes: frozen trajectory artifact for offline scoring
loops.stop_condition: Stop the trajectory at success, illegal/malformed/multiple operation, truncation, defer, four reads, nine action calls, or terminal failure. Stop the whole gate on preflight/review failure or model-load failure; never retry or repair after seeing outcomes.
loops.rationale: A bounded sequential loop tests adaptive retrieval and action while making cost, invalidity, and causal use auditable.

claims.before: The project has no valid model-facing evidence that the intended recurrent memory interface can drive RML actions.
claims.after: A pass may establish only that one pinned frozen 32B model can use supplied target-independent connected rows to solve nested J/P diagnostic targets through the registered recurrent interface, with behavior disrupted by registered cuts and redirected by twin memory.
claims.evidence_needed: All leak, call-budget, positive-control, negative-control, path-citation, cut, twin, independent-review, and frozen-artifact gates pass in the single no-retry 234-call run.

claims.before: A large end-to-end organism run was treated as the next route to the paper claim.
claims.after: G1 supplied-gold action use must pass before G2 experience-derived text; G2 must pass before G3 LoRA; only independent multi-life G4/G5 can support paper claims about learning, compression, scaling, saturation, or a flywheel.
claims.evidence_needed: Separate prospective, ratified, reviewed evidence at every rung; this change supplies G1 only.

cells.reason: The renderer emits the sealed public target and ordinary public state only.
The service keys rows by public entity identifiers but cannot use hidden answer fields.
The agent must observe its target and current public state to act.
The environment advances from the same public target and submitted actions.
The scorer replays and checks the frozen public trajectory.
Target rendering must be invariant to memory condition.
The service applies the preassigned NONE/GOLD/ATOMS/CUT/TWIN projection and logs exact returns.
Only rows returned to emitted keys are visible; unopened rows remain hidden.
Memory cannot change world dynamics or public feedback.
The scorer needs the frozen condition projection to test citations and interventions.
The renderer derives public bytes from the sealed fixture but cannot expose hidden truth.
Rows are frozen from the registered condition before scoring and cannot use model outcomes.
No truth, solution, score, verifier verdict, or counterfactual answer may enter cognition.
The environment uses hidden dynamics only to produce ordinary public consequences.
Hidden truth is released only after the model trajectory is immutable.
Rendered target bytes are identical across conditions and cannot depend on earlier model results.
The service receives a sealed projection identifier but emits no label or contrast description.
The model receives neither arm name, contrast, threshold, nor any prior result.
World transitions are condition-blind.
The offline analysis joins frozen outcomes to the preregistered assignments.

acceptance_tests.setup: Exhaustively render every condition and operation-state combination, compare target bytes across arms/twins, inspect all model-visible fields, and adversarially mutate hidden truth, labels, scores, and unopened rows.
acceptance_tests.expected: Target/state bytes are arm-invariant; only queried authorized rows differ; hidden truth, answers, labels, scores, thresholds, complete plans, and unopened rows never enter model-visible bytes; mutations are detected by tests.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: The action result could be caused by leakage or condition-specific prompting rather than memory use.

acceptance_tests.setup: Exercise the action-capable reducer with valid, malformed, multi-op, illegal, truncated, over-read, over-action, repeated-key, terminal, and simulated provider-failure outputs.
acceptance_tests.expected: Exactly one operation is accepted per call; every trajectory has at most four READ plus nine action calls, no hidden planning/retry calls, invalids score zero, and the fast registry contains exactly 18 trajectories and 234 dispatchable opportunities.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: The compute match or behavioral denominator can be changed by retries, parsing, or hidden orchestration.

acceptance_tests.setup: Run deterministic scripted good and bad policies through all 18 registered trajectories against the real RML-D0 transition engine and unchanged offline oracle.
acceptance_tests.expected: The good policy solves all GOLD_REC sides with valid cited paths, fixed-open and P atoms-only controls remain below their exact fixture ceilings, full cited cuts break credited paths, twin memory redirects predicted decisions, and bad policies fail for the registered reason.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: The harness does not faithfully instantiate the intended causal contrasts before any model call.

acceptance_tests.setup: On the intended A40 runtime, load Qwen2.5-32B revision 5ede1c97bbab6ce5cda5812749b4c0bdf79b18dd and dispatch one predeclared non-scientific grammar canary before exposing any registered target.
acceptance_tests.expected: The pinned model loads, emits one schema-valid operation under the runtime token settings, records environment and revision hashes, and consumes zero scientific opportunities.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: The frozen run is being launched against an unverified or incompatible model runtime.

acceptance_tests.setup: Execute the frozen 18-trajectory assignment once with no retries: NONE_REC, GOLD_OPEN, and GOLD_REC on all four target sides; ATOMS_REC on both P sides; CUT_REC and TWIN_REC on canonical J and P H-sides. Score only after every trajectory freezes.
acceptance_tests.expected: GOLD_REC action success is at least .85 with valid cited-path rate at least .80; NONE_REC is at most .35; GOLD_OPEN is at most .45; P ATOMS_REC is at most .35; at least .80 of credited GOLD_REC successes lose path validity under complete cited cuts and redirect in the predicted twin-memory direction; unsupported release and residue are zero.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: Correct connected memory does not causally improve action through the intended recurrent interface or the fixture lacks headroom.

acceptance_tests.setup: A fresh reviewer and separate author-side advocate inspect the frozen source, prompt, schemas, assignments, manifests, CPU artifacts, call ledger, and proposed interpretation before GPU; after the run, they review immutable outputs without repairing them.
acceptance_tests.expected: Both pre-GPU roles approve exact bytes; no actor overlap is concealed; result labels state single deterministic fixture, nested targets, supplied-gold memory, and diagnostic-only status; no DREAM, LoRA, learning, scaling, saturation, benchmark, or paper claim is emitted.
acceptance_tests.falsifies: The experiment can silently expand scope, self-certify, or be promoted beyond its evidential unit.

human_boundary.decision_question: Authorize only the RML-G1 supplied-gold recurrent action fast falsifier and its single no-retry 234-call 32B GPU gate, with DREAM, LoRA, lifetime, scaling, and paper claims explicitly excluded?
forbidden_before_approval: edit or execute the RML Stage-B model-facing implementation
create or dispatch any scientific model opportunity
launch the 32B model canary or GPU gate
state a learning, DREAM, LoRA, benchmark, scaling, saturation, flywheel, or paper result
